title: Chicken Jalfrezi
subtitle: Quick stir-fried curry with peppers
excerpt: A quick, vibrant curry of chicken strips and mixed peppers in a punchy tomato and chilli sauce. Jalfrezi is cooked at a high heat and served with a slightly charred edge to the vegetables, distinguishing it from slower-cooked curries.
sourceNotes: Jalfrezi is believed to have roots in the British Raj period, where the technique of frying leftover cooked meat with fresh spices and vegetables was used. In the modern British curry house tradition, it is typically one of the hotter dishes on the menu.

content.text: High heat is what makes a jalfrezi. The wok needs to be very hot before any ingredients go in, so the chicken and peppers colour rather than steam. Have everything prepared before you begin cooking because the process moves quickly.

Heat the wok over a high heat until smoking. Add 2 tbsp oil and the chicken strips in a single layer. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes without stirring until coloured on one side, then stir-fry for 2 more minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 15 seconds. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes over high heat until starting to char at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger, and green chilli. Stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the peppers and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the turmeric, coriander, and tomato puree. Stir for 30 seconds, then pour in the tinned tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Return the chicken to the wok. Sprinkle over the garam masala and stir for 2 minutes until the chicken is heated through. Taste and season.
Scatter over the fresh coriander and serve with basmati rice or naan bread.

items.symptom: Vegetables are soft and steamed rather than charred.
items.cause: Wok was not hot enough or was overcrowded.
items.fix: Use highest heat; cook in batches if the wok is not large.

items.symptom: Sauce is too dry and catching on the wok.
items.cause: Not enough liquid from the tinned tomatoes as they cooked.
items.fix: Add 50ml water and stir to loosen.

items.cause: It was overcooked in the initial high-heat fry.
items.fix: Cook chicken until just white; it finishes when returned to sauce.
